vault.export.dialog.format_help: Choose a portable file. A .zip is an ordinary zip of the encrypted vault (no zip password). A .7z encrypts the files with 7-Zip — easier to open elsewhere, weaker against offline password guessing. A plain-text .zip is not encrypted at all: it takes your files out as they are.

vault.export.dialog.plain_zip_password_h: Unlocks the vault so its files can be written out. The .zip itself has no password.

vault.export.option.seven_zip_desc: + Opens in 7-Zip / ZArchiver. − Weaker offline guessing than a .zip of the encrypted vault. This is not how the vault rests on disk.
vault.export.option.plain_zip_desc: Not encrypted. Anyone who gets this file can read everything in the vault, with no password. Cloud sync, backups, and the system may copy it, and deleting it later may not erase it. Use it to take your data out, and keep it only as long as you need it.

vault.create.option.import_folder_note: The files in this folder, including subfolders, are encrypted into the new vault.
vault.create.option.import_folder_dot_no: Names that start with a dot may not be included. The folder listing does not always show them.
vault.create.extract_hint: Unpack the archive into the vault. Off stores the archive as one file.

vault.create.keep_settings_hint: Fills the name, note, hint, and other options when this file carries them. Off leaves them as you set them here.
vault.create.settings_locked: These fields are locked until you test the password on the Password step. This .7z may carry its own settings: test it first, then come back here to review them.
vault.create.option.scratch_desc: Start with an empty vault and a new password.

vault.create.password_wrap_intro: Choose the password for the new vault. Optional hint is a reminder — never the password itself.
vault.create.password_settings_read: This .7z carries vault settings. They now fill the other steps, and you can still change them.
vault.create.password_no_settings: This .7z has no vault settings. Choose them on the other steps.

modal.help.title: Help
modal.help.hint: Short guides for Upriv. Search filters sections in the current language.
modal.help.body.overview.1: Upriv manages encrypted vaults. At rest each vault keeps ciphertext on disk (Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305). You can copy that encrypted vault into an ordinary .zip (recommended) or export a portable .7z.
modal.help.body.overview.2: A vault is open (you edit files) or closed (encrypted on disk). The list shows the current state with a colored badge. Recovery appears if close did not finish cleanly.
modal.help.body.overview.3: By default, files stay encrypted on disk while the vault is open. On desktop you work through a virtual folder; on mobile, through the in-app file manager. Plaintext is not written to ordinary disk in the default mode.
modal.help.body.vault_list.1: The home screen lists every vault in your Upriv root folder. Use the sort menu to order by position, name, state, or last accessed.
modal.help.body.vault_list.2: The view menu switches how vaults are shown: default rows, large cards, compact rows, or block tiles. Sort and view preferences are remembered in system settings.
modal.help.body.vault_list.3: When sorted by position, drag the handle on a row to reorder vaults. Refresh reloads the vault list from disk. With more than one vault open, More options includes Close all vaults: each one joins the close queue. If there is unsaved text, a prompt saves or discards it and only then each vault joins that queue.
modal.help.body.open_close.1: Unlock asks for the vault password. While unlocking or locking, the row shows Opening or Closing with a time budget, and Backing up while the close backup is being written. Lock flushes the session into the encrypted vault using the open session — it does not ask for the password again. Plaintext-on-disk vaults ask you to confirm before wiping the folder.
modal.help.body.open_close.2: Lock always closes. Optional idle auto-close locks after inactivity.
modal.help.body.open_close.3: Export is a separate action: copy the encrypted vault into an ordinary .zip, or stream a portable .7z. This vault must be closed; other vaults can stay open.
modal.help.body.vault_settings.1: Open settings from a vault row gear menu: Preferences (name, unlocked folder, backups, idle auto-close), Password, Unlock RAM, Storage (encrypted or plain text, with the password), and Group (assign this vault). Its last entry, Delete vault, opens a window of its own. Compression for a portable .7z is chosen when you export.
modal.help.body.vault_settings.2: Save writes config.toml on disk. Some options apply on the next unlock or close. Change password gives the vault a new key and rewrites every file with it; Back up first keeps a copy under the current password when there is room. Later backups use the new password.
modal.help.body.backups.1: When enabled, Upriv copies the encrypted vault into its backup folder on close: the data folder, or a folder from the vault's or the app's list on this device. When that folder cannot take the backup, the next one in the list does. Each backup keeps the password from when it was created.
modal.help.body.backups.2: Open Backups from a vault row to list saves (never auto-deleted) and standard backups (rotated per keep-last), export, delete, or create a new vault from a backup (+ icon; that copy is the snapshot, so the source vault can stay open). Use Save on a standard backup to pin it, or give it a name, which pins it too. Deleting requires typing the vault id to confirm.
modal.help.body.system_settings.1: System settings (⋯ menu) control Language, General (theme, header ⋮), Unlocked folders, Backups, Vault list (toolbar and row buttons), Groups (dragging vaults into groups), logging, and hidden vaults. Language changes UI strings only — vault content is unchanged.
modal.help.body.system_settings.2: To copy a vault to another drive or machine, close it, then use Export on that vault’s row. Choose a .zip of the encrypted vault (recommended) or a .7z file, and the folder it goes in. Each kind remembers its folder until you quit. There is no bulk download of several vaults at once.
modal.help.body.data_folder.1: Data folder (⋯ menu) chooses where Upriv stores `.upriv/` — settings.toml, vaults/, and logs/. It is not an individual vault. Each device keeps its own list of folders: Default is beside the program for a portable copy, the account user-data directory for an installed app, and Documents/Upriv on Android. When the selected folder does not answer at launch, Upriv opens the next one in the list that does and says so. On Android the system screen opens on Documents, which already exists; confirm it and Upriv creates the Upriv folder inside. `.upriv/` is not stored in the app private folder.
modal.help.body.data_folder.2: Export a copy, the last choice in the Data folder window, saves the whole `.upriv/` as one zip, with every vault and backup. Vault files stay encrypted. Unzipped, it holds <name>/<folder>/.upriv/: a folder named like the file (upriv-<date> unless you change it), holding the data folder under its own name (Upriv on a phone). Choose that inner folder in Data folder to use the copy. Every vault must be closed or in recovery while it runs.
modal.help.body.logs.1: View logs (⋯ menu) lists plain-text diagnostic files under `.upriv/logs`. Deleting the active file starts a new one automatically when logging continues.
modal.help.body.logs.2: Open a file to read parsed lines, or select entries to download a zip or delete old logs. Log level in system settings controls how much is written.
modal.help.body.security.1: Session keys live in RAM while a vault is open. The password string stays in RAM too after a successful unlock, until you quit the app or lock the vault. A wrong password or a dismissed attempt does not leave the password in that map. Passwords are never stored in settings files, browser storage, or log files.
modal.help.body.security.2: Encrypted directory is recommended: files stay encrypted on disk and you edit via a virtual mount or the in-app file manager. Plaintext mode writes real files while open. Previews, search indexes, Trash, backups, and app caches made while it is open can outlive the wipe. Full-disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, or LUKS) is what protects the disk after lock.
modal.help.body.security.3: An encrypted vault's unlocked folder decides who can open its files while it is open. Off keeps them in Upriv. On places a folder on this computer so other apps can open those files. They stay in memory. A plain-text vault always writes real files into its unlocked folder.
modal.help.body.recovery.1: If close did not finish, or the encrypted folder does not match the last finished close, the vault enters recovery instead of opening with no warning. For the default encrypted mode, unlock this encrypted vault again with your password. That opens the folder as it is now — a backup is not written over it.
modal.help.body.recovery.2: A plaintext vault that did not finish close keeps its folder. Remove the folder wipes it and leaves the vault closed. Files that were not saved into the encrypted vault are lost. A dead encrypted vault is restored from Backups or New vault, not from this dialog. A single corrupt file does not block the rest of the vault from opening.
unlock.title: Unlock vault
unlock.rebuild_help: Each file keeps a sealed copy of its own entry, and the list can be made again from those. A copy of the vault as it is now goes to Backups first when there is room for it. Files come back as the last close left them, and empty folders do not come back. A backup can also make a new vault.
unlock.rebuild_header_help: Each file keeps a copy of the vault's keys, locked by the password, and the header is read back from those. When the list of files is lost too, it is made again from the files' own entries. A copy of the vault as it is now goes to Backups first when there is room for it. A backup can also make a new vault.

modal.close_now.intro: This closes the vault in seconds by skipping some steps:
modal.close_now.no_backup: No backup. A backup in progress stops, and the next normal close writes one.
modal.close_now.changes_lost: Unsaved changes are lost. Everything already saved stays safe in the vault.

modal.close_now.quit_no_backup: No backup is written. The next normal close of each vault writes one.
modal.close_now.quit_changes_lost: Unsaved changes are lost, including changes other apps made in a plain-text folder that its vault has not saved yet. Everything already saved stays safe.
modal.close_now.quit_not_wiped: Plain-text folders are not wiped. Their files are deleted without being overwritten, so they can still be recovered from the disk.

modal.storage.option.upriv_plain_desc: + Real files on disk while open, for vaults too large to work on in RAM. Closed: encrypted vault only; lock always closes and wipes the folder. − Not recommended: while open, any person or app that can read the folder can read the files, and copies the system makes (previews, search, Trash) can outlast the wipe.
warning.upriv_plain: While this vault is open, its files are real files on disk. Anyone who can read that folder can read them. Previews, search, Trash, backups, and app caches made while it is open can remain after lock. Full-disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, or LUKS) protects the disk after lock. Lock saves the files into the encrypted vault and wipes them. Close and delete cannot ensure the files are completely gone from the disk.
